# 材料边界 · Materials Boundaries

Current software release: **v0.35.0** · **Natural materials and reviewed bulk ingestion** · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [MIT license](LICENSE)

A condition-aware, source-traceable materials-mechanics catalog and offline Python toolkit. It separates conditional mathematical bounds, model relations, published observations, computational predictions and synthetic demonstrations. Python 3.10+; no third-party runtime dependencies.

Repository: [chaotic-mixture/materials-boundaries-public](https://github.com/chaotic-mixture/materials-boundaries-public)

## Public-release scope

<!-- current-catalog-summary:start -->
- **41 mechanics claims**, **128 source records**, **16 observations from 5 studies**, **12 published computational predictions in 2 scientific families and 3 explicit groups**, and **5 synthetic temperature demos with 7 branches**
- Exactly **8 executable composite calculation rules**: HS/Reuss/Voigt bulk and shear bounds plus conservative derived Young's-modulus and Poisson-ratio envelopes
- Other mechanics records, including initial-yield criteria and their function comparison, scalar viscoelasticity, bulk elastic waves, hydrostatic compressibility, directional Poisson ratio, anisotropy, fatigue, fracture, stability and porous relations, are catalog-only
- The 128 sources comprise 127 bibliographic/source records plus 1 original synthetic-demo provenance record; a source record is not a redistribution of its publication or dataset
- All five temperature demos use intentionally invented coefficients and ranges. They do not describe real materials, measured properties or engineering allowables
<!-- current-catalog-summary:end -->

## Concrete material references

<!-- material-catalog-summary:start -->
The separate reference catalogue contains **1168 material identities**, **31 qualified grades**, **1169 source-scoped states** and **1180 reference properties**. Counts describe this registry only; aliases, categories, prior observations and computational model cells are not additional materials.
<!-- material-catalog-summary:end -->

The local experimental Ewurum R-series append adds four source-qualified reactive PBS/lignin formulations and four measured Young's moduli, reusing an unchanged existing source. The experimental project total is **1192 = 1168 source-qualified identities + 24 reviewed computed records**; published main remains **1081**. [Evidence, conditions and count boundaries](docs/MATERIAL_GROWTH_EWURUM_REACTIVE_20261025.md).

The five primary classes are metal, inorganic, polymer, composite and natural biological tissues/fibers. The exact reviewed v2 batch adds 1,000 distinct historical WFO species identities, each with one selected-accession conversion-derived basic-density property. The 2026-10-19 experimental core snapshot (data commit `5396fd1cc9df72507785a112a21c2990fb4a7c50`) has natural 1,010; metal 22, inorganic 26, polymer 15 and composite 10. Only natural reaches the 1,000-per-class goal in this snapshot. Ten existing biological identities migrate to natural through an exact versioned ledger. Processed biopolymers remain polymer; minerals and rocks remain inorganic. A material counts once by its admitted canonical identity, irrespective of aliases, states or measurements.

A reusable offline pipeline separates proposed, held and source-supported candidates from explicit reviewed admission. The first conversion profile preserves measured air-dry specific gravity and source-deposited basic-density estimates, their assumptions and provenance. It never turns a selected collection accession into a species mean or engineering design value. The eight executable scientific rules remain unchanged. [Guide](docs/MATERIAL_REFERENCE_CATALOG.md) · [Taxonomy](docs/MATERIAL_TAXONOMY.md) · [Bulk workflow](docs/BULK_INGESTION.md) · [Scientific gates](docs/BULK_INGESTION_DESIGN.md) · [Coverage](docs/MATERIAL_COVERAGE_v0.35.0.md) · [Migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.35.0.md)

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries coverage --text --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries catalog materials --text --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries catalog materials --category polymer --text --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog reference-properties --quantity mass_density --text --lang ja
python -m materials_boundaries catalog materials --query "graphite" --text --lang de
```

## Start with one composite case

Version **0.28.2** corrects the Reuss shear citation (Kochmann–Milton Eq. 133 is translated bulk compliance) and records the completed Meille–Garboczi Eq. 3 visual identity check. Three affected claim records advance to 1.1.1; numerical formulas and outputs, applicability gates and all eight rules are unchanged. No independent scientific review or joint-sharpness proof is added. Previously exported reports remain historical and fail current strict replay; regenerate explicitly from retained original inputs. See [evidence correction and migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.28.2.md).

Version **0.28.1** adds composite input/report saving on local Windows NTFS drives, with explicit refusal of reparse points, network/device paths and unsupported filesystems. POSIX safeguards and all scientific/report contracts are unchanged. See [Windows support and limitations](docs/COMPOSITE_WORKFLOW.md#filesystem-guarantees-and-limitations) and the [compatibility migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.28.1.md). Native Windows CI must pass for the exact release candidate before its Windows behavior is considered verified.

Version **0.28.0** turns the existing eight rules into one offline researcher workflow: explicit blank/terminal intake, a condition-and-evidence report for the supplied fractions, and closed software replay verification. It adds **no scientific records or rules**. Unknowns, partial availability, source gaps and independent-review=false stay visible. A successful replay does not verify a specimen or prove a theorem. [Workflow and safe-export contract](docs/COMPOSITE_WORKFLOW.md) · [Migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.28.0.md)

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries composite init --output case.json --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries composite init --original-demo --output demo.json --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries composite report demo.json --output demo-report --unit GPa --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries composite verify demo-report/bundle.json --json
```

The first command leaves observations unknown; `--interactive` requires a terminal and an explicit save. The second deliberately uses original fictitious data. Read conditions and evidence before interpreting approximate numbers. Output stays local in a new/empty directory; no source assets or network reads are used. HTML/text support en/zh/ja/de, while machine JSON is language-independent. ## Earlier releases

### v0.32.0 material-reference expansion

The prior 34 identities remain unchanged. This release adds nine source-qualified materials: AZ91D and AZ31 magnesium alloys, annealed 99.9% zinc, NBS molybdenum and tungsten tubes, flax and hemp technical-fiber bundles, Bombyx mori silk fibroin and Latxa sheep wool. Each identity contributes one selected numerical property. Source-specific grades, processing, populations and unknown conditions remain explicit.

A closed generic metadata extension preserves reported CV, graphical SD with unavailable numerical amplitude, SD with unnamed central aggregation, and separate relative SEM and approximate estimated inaccuracy. ### Earlier mechanics and workflow releases

Version **0.27.0** appends exactly three catalog-only records: von Mises and Tresca initial-yield relations, plus the sharp **1 <= q_T/q_VM <= 2/sqrt(3)** function comparison for the same nonhydrostatic symmetric 3D Cauchy stress tensor. The ratio is undefined at hydrostatic stress; the division-free inequality includes it. Source definitions are distinguished from original project proof and from restricted isotropic, pressure-insensitive initial-yield model applicability. Any model-threshold comparison requires the same positive uniaxial Y; an optional loading consequence is limited to one fixed local proportional ray. No numerical plasticity integration, material yield value, universal strength bracket or safety certification is added. Claims schema advances **1.12.0 → 1.13.0**; the eight executable rules remain unchanged. [Scientific scope, exact proof and source rights](docs/YIELD_CRITERIA.md) · [v0.27.0 migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.27.0.md)

Version **0.26.0** previously appended exactly two catalog-only scalar viscoelastic records and two source records. Within a matched causal linear time-invariant scalar channel, fixed material state and temperature, nonzero completely monotone ordinary relaxation with finite positive R0, and no additive Newtonian impulse, the normalized creep-relaxation convolution equals 1. The original project proof gives **0<R(t)J(t)<=1 at every finite t>0**; it is not a separately printed Hanyga theorem or a universal material-strength law. Initial jumps and possibly unbounded but integrable J' are retained. Changing loading rates remain allowed under the fixed kernel. Claims schema advances **1.11.0 → 1.12.0**; all eight executable rules are unchanged. [Scope, original proofs and source versions](docs/SCALAR_VISCOELASTICITY.md) · [v0.26.0 migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.26.0.md)

Version **0.25.0** adds one explicit `observation compare-temperature-studies --profile-id ciganas-zach-uts-temperature-v1` view. Both protocols and caveats come first; six Ciganas unspecified-central UTS summaries and four Zach reported medians remain separate, unconnected panels with always-visible SD columns. No uncertainty endpoints, matched-condition inference, pooling or ranking is added. Zach SD units remain contextual. No scientific records, old fixtures/examples, generic inspection or existing Ciganas plot policy change. [Two-study guide](docs/OBSERVATION_STUDY_COMPARISON.md) · [v0.25.0 migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.25.0.md)

Version **0.24.0** adds four catalog-only annealed ±45° PAHT-CF median UTS observations from Zach and Dudescu (2025), at reported chamber conditions 25, 50, 100 and 150 °C. Reported medians and separate SD strings are preserved; the SD unit is contextually inferred as MPa because its header prints no unit. Conditional SI scaling is explicitly labeled. No median ± SD interval, new plot, pooled estimate, interpolation or cross-study ranking is admitted. Four-language inspection shows source-specific warnings before values. All older records, fixtures, generated examples and the Ciganas plot profile remain unchanged. [Source and limits](docs/PAHT_CF_ANNEALED_OBSERVATIONS.md) · [v0.24.0 migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.24.0.md)

Version **0.23.0** adds an explicit `observation plot-temperature` route for the complete six-cell dataset `ciganas-2026-pa12-cf15-fff-uts-temperature`. Six unconnected, equally styled source-reported central UTS dots and visible ±reported-SD whiskers use numeric chamber-temperature/MPa axes, with the exact source strings alongside. Centers are not asserted means; SD is not SEM, a confidence interval, observed min–max or bounds, and the three tests per condition have unverified independence. Chamber temperature is not direct specimen temperature; absent x whiskers mean unreported uncertainty. Fixed display margins are not material limits. The new closed plot schema is **1.0.0**; generic inspection stays text-only under **1.1.0**, observations stay **1.3.0**, all records stay catalog-only, and the eight executable rules and scientific catalogs are unchanged. There is no arbitrary pressure-record admission, fit, interpolation, overlay, material prediction or allowable. [Plot/API/export contract](docs/OBSERVATION_TEMPERATURE_PLOT.md) · [v0.23.0 migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.23.0.md)

Version **0.22.0** previously added six **catalog-only PA12 CF15 tensile-test summaries** from one study, one printed-material protocol and six reported chamber conditions: **23, 40, 60, 80, 100 and 120 °C**. They are 3D ultimate tensile strength **as reported**, with source MPa strings and reported SD kept separate from exact SI Pa unit re-expression. Three tensile tests are reported per condition; the central statistic, stress convention, stress-area basis and actual moisture remain unknown. Chamber conditions are not verified direct specimen temperatures. No interpolation, continuous temperature model, confidence interval, universal strength bound or engineering allowable is added. The six older 2D records remain unchanged. Observations schema advances **1.2.0 → 1.3.0** and inspection schema **1.0.0 → 1.1.0**; saved inspection bundles must be regenerated. Version **0.21.0** previously appended exactly six **Ni11X periodic-model ideal-shear predictions** from Shimanek et al., arXiv:2108.06412v2, Table 2, p. 27: **Cr 4.90, Mn 5.12, Fe 5.20, Cu 4.51, Si 4.17 and Ti 4.24 GPa**. Unknown temperature, pressure, magnetism and uncertainty remain unknown; bare table labels do not identify the PAW datasets or valence configurations. Perdew et al. (1992) GGA is not silently relabeled PBE; 0.08 GPa peak convergence is not an error bar. It changes no scientific record or evaluator: normalized catalog values, original source strings, source-specific warnings, uncertainty evidence, scoped sample counts and unknown conditions remain separate and traceable. Exact filters and study/quantity grouping export auditable JSON, CSV, wide/narrow SVG and script-free HTML in en/zh/ja/de. Version **0.16.0** was the first public-release baseline; earlier version labels describe development milestones. Version **0.19.0** previously appended exactly two catalog-only monolayer hBN observations and one Falin et al. (2017) source, preserving all earlier records. At that release, observations schema advanced **1.1.0 → 1.2.0** with a separate closed hBN method family; claims stay **1.11.0**, sources **1.0.0**, and evaluation **1.1.0**. Scientific schema versions are independent of the software version. [Migration and unchanged contracts](docs/MIGRATION_v0.19.0.md)

The hBN values are source-printed **289 ± 24 N/m in-plane stiffness** and **23.6 ± 1.8 N/m breaking strength**. Their SD meaning comes from the publisher-linked peer-review author response, PDF p. 8, rather than the main text's ± notation alone. **N=11 is tested sheets explicitly associated with the stiffness average**, not a verified curve or failure-event count. Stiffness uses a membrane fit; strength uses nonlinear FEM **volume-averaged stresses beneath the finite-radius indenter**, distinct from Supplementary Fig. S5's maximum Von Mises diagnostic. Finite-strain stress/strain measures remain unknown. Ambient conditions and **0.5 μm/s probe translation velocity** do not supply numerical environment values or strain rate. The source formula q=1/(1.049−0.15ν−0.16ν²), ν=0.211 gives **0.9898768854482001 by curator arithmetic only**; no separately printed numerical q or actual fit constant is verified, so no hBN q discrepancy is asserted. No thickness conversion, refit, comparison or ranking is added. [Full source, method and statistical limits](docs/OBSERVATIONS.md#monolayer-hbn-falin-et-al-2017-new-records)

Version **0.18.0** previously added the two bulk elastic-wave claims and two sources, with claims schema **1.10.0 → 1.11.0**. [Its migration notes](docs/MIGRATION_v0.18.0.md) and scientific distinctions remain applicable.

For finite positive isotropic K, G and density ρ, c_L²=(K+4G/3)/ρ and c_T²=G/ρ. The material-class ratio is **c_L/c_T ∈ (√(4/3),∞)**: the lower infimum is unattained and no finite class-wide upper bound exists. Each fixed material has finite direction-independent speeds and twofold transverse degeneracy. The canonical acoustic tensor **Q_ik=C_ijkl n_j n_l** has pressure units; **Γ=Q/ρ** has speed-squared units. Strict strong ellipticity means every directional Q is SPD; full symmetric-strain energy SPD implies it, but the converse fails. Phase normal and polarization are distinct, and no generic anisotropic exact L/T ordering, ray/group-speed claim or automatic static/isothermal-modulus substitution is made. [Definitions, original proofs, source/version limits and exclusions](docs/BULK_ELASTIC_WAVES.md)

Version **0.17.0** previously added one MoS2 study and two catalog-only 2D summaries, with observations schema **1.0.0 → 1.1.0**. [Its migration notes](docs/MIGRATION_v0.17.0.md) remain applicable.

The retained monolayer MoS2 summaries are **180 ± 60 N/m in-plane stiffness** and **15 ± 3 N/m breaking strength**, with source-reported standard deviations. They retain a flagged inconsistency between the printed q formula and stated q = 0.95; the actual fit constant remains unresolved. The inspected EPFL artifact is proof-formatted (A–G); final publisher text and the supplement are unverified. No refit, plot, comparison, ranking or thickness conversion is added. [Observation evidence and limits](docs/OBSERVATIONS.md#monolayer-mos2-bertolazzi-et-al-2011-new-records)

Original project code, documentation and original curation are MIT-licensed under the maintainer handle **chaotic-mixture**. This does not relicense third-party publications, source datasets or scientific facts, or imply their authors' endorsement. See [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [source provenance](docs/SOURCES.md).

The five NIST cryogenic coefficient datasets and all derived examples are omitted conservatively while reuse terms are clarified. This is not a finding that redistribution is prohibited. Bibliographic records and official links remain. The collection is currently listed by NIST as a curated collection, formerly SRD 152; reclassification alone does not establish an express redistribution grant. [Details and official sources](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md#nist-cryogenic-material-properties)

Formula checks and software tests do not constitute independent scientific peer review or validate a real specimen. Scientific and native-language review remain incomplete; the catalog is not comprehensive.

## Quick start

```sh
python -m pip install -e .
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --id isotropic_bulk_plane_wave_speeds_and_ratio --text --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --query compressibility --text --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries catalog observations --source-id falin_et_al_2017_hbn_mechanical_properties --text --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries catalog observations --source-id ciganas2026polym18050563 --text --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries observation inspect --source-id ciganas2026polym18050563 --output /tmp/pa12-cf15 --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries observation inspect --output /tmp/observations --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries observation plot-temperature --dataset-id ciganas-2026-pa12-cf15-fff-uts-temperature --output /tmp/pa12-temperature-plot --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries catalog predictions --text --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries prediction plot --group-id shimanek_v2_table2_cr_mn_fe_cu_si_ti --output /tmp/ni11x-six --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries temperature evaluate examples/temperature/synthetic-linear-50k.json --json
python -m materials_boundaries temperature evaluate examples/temperature/synthetic-overlap-50k.json --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries temperature plot --output /tmp/temperature-demo --lang en
```

The synthetic linear temperature demo returns **15 GPa at 50 K**. The overlap demo returns **25 and 32.5 GPa at 50 K**, retaining both artificial branches. These are invented demonstration outputs, not NIST results or material-property data. Outside the authored ranges, no value is extrapolated. ## 立即运行

Python 3.10+，运行时无第三方依赖。在仓库根目录：

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang ja
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang de
```

也可安装命令行入口：

```sh
python -m pip install -e .
materials-boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang zh
```

同一份公式、单位、数据标识符和原始引用供四种语言共用。`--lang` 只改变可读标签/说明；JSON、错误代码、条件标识符及 CLI 参数保持稳定英文。`--lang` 可放在命令前或命令后，重复指定时以最后一次为准；`--help` 的标签/说明也随之切换，命令语法和标识符不变。翻译尚未经过独立科学或母语审校。

## 合成示例的预期结果

输入全为人为构造的演示数值，**不是测量结果、文献材料参数或 Materials Project 记录**：

- 第一相：K₁ = 10 GPa，G₁ = 5 GPa，体积分数 f₁ = 0.5
- 第二相：K₂ = 30 GPa，G₂ = 15 GPa，体积分数 f₂ = 0.5
- 体积模量 K：HS 为 16.25–17.5 GPa；Reuss / Voigt 为 15 / 20 GPa
- 剪切模量 G：HS 约为 8.37837837838–9.04761904762 GPa；Reuss / Voigt 为 7.5 / 10 GPa
- 杨氏模量 E 推导外包络：约 21.4488468362–23.1528046422 GPa
- 泊松比 ν 推导外包络：约 0.265190525232–0.293562708102，无量纲单位 `1`

这些结果是数值近似，不是某个具体微结构的性能预测，也不是区间算术认证的端点。E/ν 是由分别成立的 K/G 界推导的**保守外包络，不是紧的联合可达界**；两个 HS 端点不一定能由同一微结构同时达到。

E = 9KG/(3K+G)，ν = (3K−2G)/(2(3K+G))。E 下/上端点分别使用 (Klow,Glow)/(Khigh,Ghigh)，ν 下/上端点使用 (Klow,Ghigh)/(Khigh,Glow)。推导仅使用同一输入体系的 HS 体积/剪切模量结果，并保留依赖论断与实例 ID；前提未知或不满足时不输出数值，相排序不一致时不回退到 Reuss/Voigt。

## 首个文献模型示例

`examples/literature-epoxy-glass-model.json` 使用 [Genin–Birman 2009](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijsolstr.2008.08.010) 的环氧/玻璃组分模型参数。它与仓库中的合成示例分开标记为 `literature_model`，并非测量材料或已报告试样。

原始 E/ν、K/G 换算方法和文献定位均保留；玻璃 20% / 环氧 80% 是计算示例的选择。宏观各向同性、理想粘结等作为计算器假设记录，温度、牌号、固化状态和测量不确定性保持未知。条件成立时体积模量 HS 约为 5.59472–9.40776 GPa，Reuss / Voigt 约为 5.30327 / 13.6 GPa。v0.2.0 同时输出剪切界和有效 E/ν 外包络；这些有效材料输出与原始组分 E/ν 不是同一物理记录。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/literature-epoxy-glass-model.json --lang zh
```

[完整来源、假设与换算说明](docs/LITERATURE_EXAMPLE.md)。该来源保留所有版权；仓库不附论文全文、PDF 或图。

## 复合材料计算器支持的条件

- 三维、小应变、静态、线性弹性
- **组分各向同性** `constituent_symmetry` 与**宏观有效各向同性** `effective_symmetry` 分别声明；后者不能代替前者
- 理想粘结 `perfectly_bonded`
- 两相描述，已知体积分数；活动相 K > 0 且 G > 0
- HS 及依赖 HS 的 E/ν 外包络额外要求 well-ordered：K 与 G 的相排序一致；排序保留每相 K/G/体积分数配对，包含相等模量极限
- 允许 f = 0 / 1 的纯相极限；不存在相的未知参数不参与计算

Reuss / Voigt 比较使用同一保守条件集合，但不要求 well-ordered。更一般定理可适用的情况，不代表本实现也支持。负刚度、活动孔隙/零刚度相、各向异性组分、非理想界面、动态/有限应变、强度/失效/塑性数值评价和联合可达域均未实现。断裂、稳定性、孔隙论断及独立观测记录只保存目录知识，不扩大该计算器的适用范围。

## 三态与输入验证

- `satisfied`：提供的声明/数值满足本实现条件；不表示已验证实际材料
- `violated`：至少一个已知条件不匹配；不表示这种材料不可能存在
- `unknown`：没有已知冲突，但至少一个必要条件/参数未知

缺失观察量或 `null` 保持未知，绝不替换成 0 或无穷大。`violated` 优先于 `unknown`，输出保留所有逐条件证据。仅 `satisfied` 的 claim 产生数值。非有限值、错误单位、重复键/相 ID、非法类型和不一致体积分数会报输入错误。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries validate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/unknown-isotropy.json --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/anisotropic-constituent.json --json
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --unit MPa --json
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims
python -m materials_boundaries catalog sources
```

退出码：0 = 完成验证/评价（包括 unknown / violated）或目录查询（包括空结果），2 = 无效输入/CLI 用法或未知记录 ID，3 = 数值输出范围错误。模量输出单位支持 `Pa`、`kPa`、`MPa`、`GPa`；每个输入模量独立带单位，内部统一为 Pa。泊松比始终以无量纲单位 `1` 输出，不随 `--unit` 换算，也不能把 `1` 用作该参数值。ν 必须严格满足 −1 < ν < 0.5；负值与零值可有效。若浮点舍入落在任一不包含的边界，返回 `numerical_range_error` 和 null，不裁剪为物理端点。依赖的 HS 结果发生数值错误时，推导结果也不可用。

`catalog claims`、`catalog sources` 和新增 `catalog observations` 默认输出规范 JSON，兼容现有调用；`--json` 显式选择相同格式。使用 `--text --lang zh|en|ja|de` 阅读本地化标签和证据状态说明，原始标题、证据文字及规范 ID 保留。搜索仅检查仓库随附的人工策展记录，不联网、不修改记录，也不评价材料输入。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --id hs_bulk_3d_two_phase --text --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries --lang ja catalog claims --direction interval --text
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --query "bulk kochmann" --source-id kochmann_milton_2014 --json

python -m materials_boundaries --lang zh catalog --help
```

- `--id` 精确匹配记录 ID，区分大小写；未知 ID 报错并以 2 退出
- `--query` 按空白拆词，经 Unicode `casefold` 后做字面子串匹配，所有词均须命中。检索 ID、标题/名称，以及来源的作者、DOI、用途；论断还检索物理量、方向、`claim_type`、规则 ID 和证据来源 ID。观测检索 ID、名称、物理量、`observation_type`、`study_id`、`material.name` 和证据来源 ID；十八条 v0.4.0–v0.6.0、v0.8.0 与 v0.9.0 论断及六条观测的人工策展四语言显示名称也作为字面搜索别名；它不搜索论文全文，不做词干化、排名、模糊匹配或自动翻译
- `claims` 专用筛选：`--direction interval|lower|upper|prediction|relation|constraint`、`--claim-type theoretical_bound|derived_outer_envelope|model_estimate|model_relation|stability_criterion`
- 论断与观测共用 `--source-id`（精确匹配证据引用的来源 ID）；观测专用 `--quantity` 和 `--observation-type experiment_derived_model_dependent|experiment_derived_tensile_test_summary`

阅读记录、核对公式或软件测试均不构成独立科学证明，也不授予来源内容的再使用许可。许可证筛选仅匹配已记录的元数据。检索到一条论断不代表它适用于某个材料；检索不到也不代表不存在相关文献或定理。

## v0.8.0：四方／菱方严格稳定性模板

四条新记录沿用来源的 I／II 名称与 Laue 类：`tetragonal_i_born_stability`（4/mmm，6 个独立常数）、`tetragonal_ii_born_stability`（4/m，7 个）、`rhombohedral_i_born_stability`（−3m，6 个）、`rhombohedral_ii_born_stability`（−3，7 个）。菱方在此也称三方；不是要求使用非正交原胞坐标。

四条判据共同要求 C11 > |C12|、C33(C11+C12) − 2C13² > 0、C44 > 0，另分别要求：

- 四方 I：C66 > 0
- 四方 II：C66(C11−C12) − 2C16² > 0
- 菱方 I：C44(C11−C12) − 2C14² > 0
- 菱方 II：C44(C11−C12) − 2(C14²+C15²) > 0

四方两类的 C66 独立；菱方两类必须满足 C66=(C11−C12)/2。采用右手正交 Cartesian 坐标、z 沿主四重／三重轴；I 类 x 沿基面 Laue 二重轴，II 类保留固定基面方向中的允许耦合。Voigt 次序为 (xx,yy,zz,yz,xz,xy)，应变剪切项乘 2，应力剪切项不乘 2。完整矩阵与符号约定必须匹配，不能删去破坏对称性的项或单独改耦合符号。

这些严格不等式仅在**无应力平衡态、均匀无穷小应变、谐波二次能量**及对应完整实对称模板内为充要条件。菱方 II 的两个耦合须合并检查，分别通过不够；菱方行列式含耦合余量的平方，正行列式也不够。等号不满足严格稳定性；只有整个矩阵半正定且存在零模态时，才可称为谐波临界情况。它们不证明全声子稳定性、预应力／有限载荷稳定性或强度，近零不确定值也不自动分类。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --id tetragonal_ii_born_stability --text --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --query "rhombohedral" --text --lang en
```

## 历史 v0.6.0：各向同性固体＋孔隙界

新增 `hs_porous_bulk_3d_solid_void`、`hs_porous_shear_3d_solid_void` 和 `hs_porous_youngs_outer_3d_solid_void`。Ks、Gs 为正的固体模量，p 为孔隙体积分数；Roberts–Garboczi 原文的 p 是固相分数，须换为 1−p。完整有限孔隙率上界为：

- Kupper = 4 Ks Gs (1−p)/(4 Gs + 3 Ks p)
- Gupper = Gs (1−p)(9 Ks + 8 Gs)/(9 Ks + 8 Gs + 6 p(Ks + 2 Gs))
- Eupper = Es (1−p)/(1 + C p)，Es = 9 Ks Gs/(3 Ks + Gs)，νs = (3 Ks−2 Gs)/(2(3 Ks+Gs))，C = (1+νs)(13−15νs)/(2(7−5νs))

几何可包含不连通固体，因此 0<p<1 时三个下界为零；p=0 必须收缩为纯固体值；p=1 仅表示形式上的空域零刚度，不定义泊松比或比模量。孔隙极限采用保持宏观各向同性的正刚度趋零论证，不能直接把零代入奇异项。杨氏模量式是保守外包络，不保证同一微结构同时达到 K/G 上端点。

只有固定固体密度 ρs 且孔隙无质量时，才有 ρeff=(1−p)ρs。低密度一阶渐近式不能替代完整公式成为有限密度严格上界。来源保留精确定位、分数约定和 NIST 封面／期刊页版权声明差异，不推断普遍再使用权。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --query porous --direction interval --text --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog sources --id roberts_garboczi_2002_porous --text --lang zh
```

## 历史 v0.4.0：五条强度／断裂知识记录

- Frenkel：tau_ideal = G_slip b/(2πh)，保留特定滑移系刚度和 b/h 比值，不能直接套用多晶平均剪切模量
- UBER：sigma_max = W_sep/(e lambda)，由有来源的内聚能量模型求导；W_sep 为正分离功，局部张开量不能直接用超胞伸长量替代
- 中央裂纹：K_I = sigma sqrt(πa)，a 是完整裂纹 2a 的一半；K_I 不是断裂韧度或体积模量 K
- I 型能量关系：G_I = K_I²/E_prime；G_I 不是剪切模量 G，也不是自动给定的临界 Gc
- 有限宽度：Y = sqrt(sec(πa/W))，W 为完整板宽，采用有第二来源核对的 0 < 2a/W ≤ 0.8 范围；原来源的宽度比歧义明确保留

前两条是 `model_estimate`；后三条是新增的 `model_relation` / `direction: relation`，均为 `catalog_only`，不冒充严格理论上界，不增加数值计算器。论断目录升为 schema 1.3.0，评价仍为 schema 1.1.0。原有十条论断和十一条来源的内容保持不变。

## 历史 v0.3.0：仅目录的断裂模型

新增 `griffith_central_crack_plane_stress` 和 `griffith_central_crack_plane_strain`，分别记录平面应力／平面应变下中央贯穿裂纹的临界远场拉应力模型。两者为 `claim_type: model_estimate`、`direction: prediction`、`bound_kind: null`、`evaluation_support: catalog_only`。六条 K/G 界标为 `theoretical_bound`，E/ν 标为 `derived_outer_envelope`；旧记录的 `bound_kind` 保持不变。

σc = sqrt(E_prime Gc/(πa))，平面应力取 E_prime = E，平面应变取 E_prime = E/(1−ν²)。E 为杨氏模量（Pa），Gc 为临界能量释放率（J/m²），a 为裂纹总长 2a 的一半（m），ν 为无量纲泊松比。每条模型的 `parameters` 保存符号、物理量、量纲、SI 单位及含义。Gc 不自动等于 2γ；只有形成两个新表面是唯一耗散的理想纯脆性特例才可作此替换。

这些模型要求均匀各向同性线弹性材料、足够宽／无限大板中的中央贯穿裂纹、远场 I 型拉伸，以及足够小的屈服区／断裂过程区。它们不是普适抗拉强度上界或工程许用应力，不能外推至原子尺度或 a → 0。目录记录不证明实际前提成立，不产生实例适用性状态，也不计算应力；前提未知或违反时不能据此使用公式。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --id griffith_central_crack_plane_strain --json
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --query "model_estimate Griffith" --text --lang en
```

# 材料边界 · Materials Boundaries

Current software release: **v0.35.0** · **Natural materials and reviewed bulk ingestion** · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [MIT license](LICENSE)

A condition-aware, source-traceable materials-mechanics catalog and offline Python toolkit. It separates conditional mathematical bounds, model relations, published observations, computational predictions and synthetic demonstrations. Python 3.10+; no third-party runtime dependencies.

Repository: [chaotic-mixture/materials-boundaries-public](https://github.com/chaotic-mixture/materials-boundaries-public)

## Public-release scope

<!-- current-catalog-summary:start -->
- **41 mechanics claims**, **129 source records**, **16 observations from 5 studies**, **12 published computational predictions in 2 scientific families and 3 explicit groups**, and **5 synthetic temperature demos with 7 branches**
- Exactly **8 executable composite calculation rules**: HS/Reuss/Voigt bulk and shear bounds plus conservative derived Young's-modulus and Poisson-ratio envelopes
- Other mechanics records, including initial-yield criteria and their function comparison, scalar viscoelasticity, bulk elastic waves, hydrostatic compressibility, directional Poisson ratio, anisotropy, fatigue, fracture, stability and porous relations, are catalog-only
- The 129 sources comprise 128 bibliographic/source records plus 1 original synthetic-demo provenance record; a source record is not a redistribution of its publication or dataset
- All five temperature demos use intentionally invented coefficients and ranges. They do not describe real materials, measured properties or engineering allowables
<!-- current-catalog-summary:end -->

## Concrete material references

<!-- material-catalog-summary:start -->
The separate reference catalogue contains **1175 material identities**, **31 qualified grades**, **1176 source-scoped states** and **1187 reference properties**. Counts describe this registry only; aliases, categories, prior observations and computational model cells are not additional materials.
<!-- material-catalog-summary:end -->

The local experimental Delgado PLA/PCL append adds seven source-qualified nominal-ratio polymer blends with seven measured Young's moduli and one source. The local experimental project total is **1199 = 1175 source-qualified identities + 24 reviewed computed records**; the last published experimental baseline remains **1192** pending review and publication, and published main remains **1081**. [Evidence, conditions and count boundaries](docs/MATERIAL_GROWTH_DELGADO_PLA_PCL_20261026.md).

The five primary classes are metal, inorganic, polymer, composite and natural biological tissues/fibers. The exact reviewed v2 batch adds 1,000 distinct historical WFO species identities, each with one selected-accession conversion-derived basic-density property. The 2026-10-19 experimental core snapshot (data commit `5396fd1cc9df72507785a112a21c2990fb4a7c50`) has natural 1,010; metal 22, inorganic 26, polymer 15 and composite 10. Only natural reaches the 1,000-per-class goal in this snapshot. Ten existing biological identities migrate to natural through an exact versioned ledger. Processed biopolymers remain polymer; minerals and rocks remain inorganic. A material counts once by its admitted canonical identity, irrespective of aliases, states or measurements.

A reusable offline pipeline separates proposed, held and source-supported candidates from explicit reviewed admission. The first conversion profile preserves measured air-dry specific gravity and source-deposited basic-density estimates, their assumptions and provenance. It never turns a selected collection accession into a species mean or engineering design value. The eight executable scientific rules remain unchanged. [Guide](docs/MATERIAL_REFERENCE_CATALOG.md) · [Taxonomy](docs/MATERIAL_TAXONOMY.md) · [Bulk workflow](docs/BULK_INGESTION.md) · [Scientific gates](docs/BULK_INGESTION_DESIGN.md) · [Coverage](docs/MATERIAL_COVERAGE_v0.35.0.md) · [Migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.35.0.md)

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries coverage --text --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries catalog materials --text --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries catalog materials --category polymer --text --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog reference-properties --quantity mass_density --text --lang ja
python -m materials_boundaries catalog materials --query "graphite" --text --lang de
```

## Start with one composite case

Version **0.28.2** corrects the Reuss shear citation (Kochmann–Milton Eq. 133 is translated bulk compliance) and records the completed Meille–Garboczi Eq. 3 visual identity check. Three affected claim records advance to 1.1.1; numerical formulas and outputs, applicability gates and all eight rules are unchanged. No independent scientific review or joint-sharpness proof is added. Previously exported reports remain historical and fail current strict replay; regenerate explicitly from retained original inputs. See [evidence correction and migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.28.2.md).

Version **0.28.1** adds composite input/report saving on local Windows NTFS drives, with explicit refusal of reparse points, network/device paths and unsupported filesystems. POSIX safeguards and all scientific/report contracts are unchanged. See [Windows support and limitations](docs/COMPOSITE_WORKFLOW.md#filesystem-guarantees-and-limitations) and the [compatibility migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.28.1.md). Native Windows CI must pass for the exact release candidate before its Windows behavior is considered verified.

Version **0.28.0** turns the existing eight rules into one offline researcher workflow: explicit blank/terminal intake, a condition-and-evidence report for the supplied fractions, and closed software replay verification. It adds **no scientific records or rules**. Unknowns, partial availability, source gaps and independent-review=false stay visible. A successful replay does not verify a specimen or prove a theorem. [Workflow and safe-export contract](docs/COMPOSITE_WORKFLOW.md) · [Migration](docs/MIGRATION_v0.28.0.md)

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries composite init --output case.json --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries composite init --original-demo --output demo.json --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries composite report demo.json --output demo-report --unit GPa --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries composite verify demo-report/bundle.json --json
```

The first command leaves observations unknown; `--interactive` requires a terminal and an explicit save. The second deliberately uses original fictitious data. Read conditions and evidence before interpreting approximate numbers. Output stays local in a new/empty directory; no source assets or network reads are used. HTML/text support en/zh/ja/de, while machine JSON is language-independent. For finite positive isotropic K, G and density ρ, c_L²=(K+4G/3)/ρ and c_T²=G/ρ. The material-class ratio is **c_L/c_T ∈ (√(4/3),∞)**: the lower infimum is unattained and no finite class-wide upper bound exists. Each fixed material has finite direction-independent speeds and twofold transverse degeneracy. The canonical acoustic tensor **Q_ik=C_ijkl n_j n_l** has pressure units; **Γ=Q/ρ** has speed-squared units. Strict strong ellipticity means every directional Q is SPD; full symmetric-strain energy SPD implies it, but the converse fails. Phase normal and polarization are distinct, and no generic anisotropic exact L/T ordering, ray/group-speed claim or automatic static/isothermal-modulus substitution is made. ## 立即运行

Python 3.10+，运行时无第三方依赖。在仓库根目录：

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang en
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang ja
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang de
```

也可安装命令行入口：

```sh
python -m pip install -e .
materials-boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --lang zh
```

同一份公式、单位、数据标识符和原始引用供四种语言共用。`--lang` 只改变可读标签/说明；JSON、错误代码、条件标识符及 CLI 参数保持稳定英文。`--lang` 可放在命令前或命令后，重复指定时以最后一次为准；`--help` 的标签/说明也随之切换，命令语法和标识符不变。翻译尚未经过独立科学或母语审校。

## 合成示例的预期结果

输入全为人为构造的演示数值，**不是测量结果、文献材料参数或 Materials Project 记录**：

- 第一相：K₁ = 10 GPa，G₁ = 5 GPa，体积分数 f₁ = 0.5
- 第二相：K₂ = 30 GPa，G₂ = 15 GPa，体积分数 f₂ = 0.5
- 体积模量 K：HS 为 16.25–17.5 GPa；Reuss / Voigt 为 15 / 20 GPa
- 剪切模量 G：HS 约为 8.37837837838–9.04761904762 GPa；Reuss / Voigt 为 7.5 / 10 GPa
- 杨氏模量 E 推导外包络：约 21.4488468362–23.1528046422 GPa
- 泊松比 ν 推导外包络：约 0.265190525232–0.293562708102，无量纲单位 `1`

这些结果是数值近似，不是某个具体微结构的性能预测，也不是区间算术认证的端点。E/ν 是由分别成立的 K/G 界推导的**保守外包络，不是紧的联合可达界**；两个 HS 端点不一定能由同一微结构同时达到。

E = 9KG/(3K+G)，ν = (3K−2G)/(2(3K+G))。E 下/上端点分别使用 (Klow,Glow)/(Khigh,Ghigh)，ν 下/上端点使用 (Klow,Ghigh)/(Khigh,Glow)。推导仅使用同一输入体系的 HS 体积/剪切模量结果，并保留依赖论断与实例 ID；前提未知或不满足时不输出数值，相排序不一致时不回退到 Reuss/Voigt。

## 首个文献模型示例

`examples/literature-epoxy-glass-model.json` 使用 [Genin–Birman 2009](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijsolstr.2008.08.010) 的环氧/玻璃组分模型参数。它与仓库中的合成示例分开标记为 `literature_model`，并非测量材料或已报告试样。

原始 E/ν、K/G 换算方法和文献定位均保留；玻璃 20% / 环氧 80% 是计算示例的选择。宏观各向同性、理想粘结等作为计算器假设记录，温度、牌号、固化状态和测量不确定性保持未知。条件成立时体积模量 HS 约为 5.59472–9.40776 GPa，Reuss / Voigt 约为 5.30327 / 13.6 GPa。v0.2.0 同时输出剪切界和有效 E/ν 外包络；这些有效材料输出与原始组分 E/ν 不是同一物理记录。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/literature-epoxy-glass-model.json --lang zh
```

[完整来源、假设与换算说明](docs/LITERATURE_EXAMPLE.md)。该来源保留所有版权；仓库不附论文全文、PDF 或图。

## 复合材料计算器支持的条件

- 三维、小应变、静态、线性弹性
- **组分各向同性** `constituent_symmetry` 与**宏观有效各向同性** `effective_symmetry` 分别声明；后者不能代替前者
- 理想粘结 `perfectly_bonded`
- 两相描述，已知体积分数；活动相 K > 0 且 G > 0
- HS 及依赖 HS 的 E/ν 外包络额外要求 well-ordered：K 与 G 的相排序一致；排序保留每相 K/G/体积分数配对，包含相等模量极限
- 允许 f = 0 / 1 的纯相极限；不存在相的未知参数不参与计算

Reuss / Voigt 比较使用同一保守条件集合，但不要求 well-ordered。更一般定理可适用的情况，不代表本实现也支持。负刚度、活动孔隙/零刚度相、各向异性组分、非理想界面、动态/有限应变、强度/失效/塑性数值评价和联合可达域均未实现。断裂、稳定性、孔隙论断及独立观测记录只保存目录知识，不扩大该计算器的适用范围。

## 三态与输入验证

- `satisfied`：提供的声明/数值满足本实现条件；不表示已验证实际材料
- `violated`：至少一个已知条件不匹配；不表示这种材料不可能存在
- `unknown`：没有已知冲突，但至少一个必要条件/参数未知

缺失观察量或 `null` 保持未知，绝不替换成 0 或无穷大。`violated` 优先于 `unknown`，输出保留所有逐条件证据。仅 `satisfied` 的 claim 产生数值。非有限值、错误单位、重复键/相 ID、非法类型和不一致体积分数会报输入错误。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries validate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/unknown-isotropy.json --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/anisotropic-constituent.json --json
python -m materials_boundaries evaluate examples/synthetic-two-phase.json --unit MPa --json
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims
python -m materials_boundaries catalog sources
```

退出码：0 = 完成验证/评价（包括 unknown / violated）或目录查询（包括空结果），2 = 无效输入/CLI 用法或未知记录 ID，3 = 数值输出范围错误。模量输出单位支持 `Pa`、`kPa`、`MPa`、`GPa`；每个输入模量独立带单位，内部统一为 Pa。泊松比始终以无量纲单位 `1` 输出，不随 `--unit` 换算，也不能把 `1` 用作该参数值。ν 必须严格满足 −1 < ν < 0.5；负值与零值可有效。若浮点舍入落在任一不包含的边界，返回 `numerical_range_error` 和 null，不裁剪为物理端点。依赖的 HS 结果发生数值错误时，推导结果也不可用。

`catalog claims`、`catalog sources` 和新增 `catalog observations` 默认输出规范 JSON，兼容现有调用；`--json` 显式选择相同格式。使用 `--text --lang zh|en|ja|de` 阅读本地化标签和证据状态说明，原始标题、证据文字及规范 ID 保留。搜索仅检查仓库随附的人工策展记录，不联网、不修改记录，也不评价材料输入。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --id hs_bulk_3d_two_phase --text --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries --lang ja catalog claims --direction interval --text
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --query "bulk kochmann" --source-id kochmann_milton_2014 --json

```

- `--id` 精确匹配记录 ID，区分大小写；未知 ID 报错并以 2 退出
- `--query` 按空白拆词，经 Unicode `casefold` 后做字面子串匹配，所有词均须命中。检索 ID、标题/名称，以及来源的作者、DOI、用途；论断还检索物理量、方向、`claim_type`、规则 ID 和证据来源 ID。观测检索 ID、名称、物理量、`observation_type`、`study_id`、`material.name` 和证据来源 ID；十八条 v0.4.0–v0.6.0、v0.8.0 与 v0.9.0 论断及六条观测的人工策展四语言显示名称也作为字面搜索别名；它不搜索论文全文，不做词干化、排名、模糊匹配或自动翻译
- `claims` 专用筛选：`--direction interval|lower|upper|prediction|relation|constraint`、`--claim-type theoretical_bound|derived_outer_envelope|model_estimate|model_relation|stability_criterion`
- 论断与观测共用 `--source-id`（精确匹配证据引用的来源 ID）；观测专用 `--quantity` 和 `--observation-type experiment_derived_model_dependent|experiment_derived_tensile_test_summary`

阅读记录、核对公式或软件测试均不构成独立科学证明，也不授予来源内容的再使用许可。许可证筛选仅匹配已记录的元数据。检索到一条论断不代表它适用于某个材料；检索不到也不代表不存在相关文献或定理。

## v0.8.0：四方／菱方严格稳定性模板

四条新记录沿用来源的 I／II 名称与 Laue 类：`tetragonal_i_born_stability`（4/mmm，6 个独立常数）、`tetragonal_ii_born_stability`（4/m，7 个）、`rhombohedral_i_born_stability`（−3m，6 个）、`rhombohedral_ii_born_stability`（−3，7 个）。菱方在此也称三方；不是要求使用非正交原胞坐标。

四条判据共同要求 C11 > |C12|、C33(C11+C12) − 2C13² > 0、C44 > 0，另分别要求：

- 四方 I：C66 > 0
- 四方 II：C66(C11−C12) − 2C16² > 0
- 菱方 I：C44(C11−C12) − 2C14² > 0
- 菱方 II：C44(C11−C12) − 2(C14²+C15²) > 0

四方两类的 C66 独立；菱方两类必须满足 C66=(C11−C12)/2。采用右手正交 Cartesian 坐标、z 沿主四重／三重轴；I 类 x 沿基面 Laue 二重轴，II 类保留固定基面方向中的允许耦合。Voigt 次序为 (xx,yy,zz,yz,xz,xy)，应变剪切项乘 2，应力剪切项不乘 2。完整矩阵与符号约定必须匹配，不能删去破坏对称性的项或单独改耦合符号。

这些严格不等式仅在**无应力平衡态、均匀无穷小应变、谐波二次能量**及对应完整实对称模板内为充要条件。菱方 II 的两个耦合须合并检查，分别通过不够；菱方行列式含耦合余量的平方，正行列式也不够。等号不满足严格稳定性；只有整个矩阵半正定且存在零模态时，才可称为谐波临界情况。它们不证明全声子稳定性、预应力／有限载荷稳定性或强度，近零不确定值也不自动分类。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --id tetragonal_ii_born_stability --text --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --query "rhombohedral" --text --lang en
```

## 历史 v0.6.0：各向同性固体＋孔隙界

新增 `hs_porous_bulk_3d_solid_void`、`hs_porous_shear_3d_solid_void` 和 `hs_porous_youngs_outer_3d_solid_void`。Ks、Gs 为正的固体模量，p 为孔隙体积分数；Roberts–Garboczi 原文的 p 是固相分数，须换为 1−p。完整有限孔隙率上界为：

- Kupper = 4 Ks Gs (1−p)/(4 Gs + 3 Ks p)
- Gupper = Gs (1−p)(9 Ks + 8 Gs)/(9 Ks + 8 Gs + 6 p(Ks + 2 Gs))
- Eupper = Es (1−p)/(1 + C p)，Es = 9 Ks Gs/(3 Ks + Gs)，νs = (3 Ks−2 Gs)/(2(3 Ks+Gs))，C = (1+νs)(13−15νs)/(2(7−5νs))

几何可包含不连通固体，因此 0<p<1 时三个下界为零；p=0 必须收缩为纯固体值；p=1 仅表示形式上的空域零刚度，不定义泊松比或比模量。孔隙极限采用保持宏观各向同性的正刚度趋零论证，不能直接把零代入奇异项。杨氏模量式是保守外包络，不保证同一微结构同时达到 K/G 上端点。

只有固定固体密度 ρs 且孔隙无质量时，才有 ρeff=(1−p)ρs。低密度一阶渐近式不能替代完整公式成为有限密度严格上界。来源保留精确定位、分数约定和 NIST 封面／期刊页版权声明差异，不推断普遍再使用权。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --query porous --direction interval --text --lang zh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog sources --id roberts_garboczi_2002_porous --text --lang zh
```

## 历史 v0.4.0：五条强度／断裂知识记录

- Frenkel：tau_ideal = G_slip b/(2πh)，保留特定滑移系刚度和 b/h 比值，不能直接套用多晶平均剪切模量
- UBER：sigma_max = W_sep/(e lambda)，由有来源的内聚能量模型求导；W_sep 为正分离功，局部张开量不能直接用超胞伸长量替代
- 中央裂纹：K_I = sigma sqrt(πa)，a 是完整裂纹 2a 的一半；K_I 不是断裂韧度或体积模量 K
- I 型能量关系：G_I = K_I²/E_prime；G_I 不是剪切模量 G，也不是自动给定的临界 Gc
- 有限宽度：Y = sqrt(sec(πa/W))，W 为完整板宽，采用有第二来源核对的 0 < 2a/W ≤ 0.8 范围；原来源的宽度比歧义明确保留

前两条是 `model_estimate`；后三条是新增的 `model_relation` / `direction: relation`，均为 `catalog_only`，不冒充严格理论上界，不增加数值计算器。论断目录升为 schema 1.3.0，评价仍为 schema 1.1.0。原有十条论断和十一条来源的内容保持不变。

## 历史 v0.3.0：仅目录的断裂模型

新增 `griffith_central_crack_plane_stress` 和 `griffith_central_crack_plane_strain`，分别记录平面应力／平面应变下中央贯穿裂纹的临界远场拉应力模型。两者为 `claim_type: model_estimate`、`direction: prediction`、`bound_kind: null`、`evaluation_support: catalog_only`。六条 K/G 界标为 `theoretical_bound`，E/ν 标为 `derived_outer_envelope`；旧记录的 `bound_kind` 保持不变。

σc = sqrt(E_prime Gc/(πa))，平面应力取 E_prime = E，平面应变取 E_prime = E/(1−ν²)。E 为杨氏模量（Pa），Gc 为临界能量释放率（J/m²），a 为裂纹总长 2a 的一半（m），ν 为无量纲泊松比。每条模型的 `parameters` 保存符号、物理量、量纲、SI 单位及含义。Gc 不自动等于 2γ；只有形成两个新表面是唯一耗散的理想纯脆性特例才可作此替换。

这些模型要求均匀各向同性线弹性材料、足够宽／无限大板中的中央贯穿裂纹、远场 I 型拉伸，以及足够小的屈服区／断裂过程区。它们不是普适抗拉强度上界或工程许用应力，不能外推至原子尺度或 a → 0。目录记录不证明实际前提成立，不产生实例适用性状态，也不计算应力；前提未知或违反时不能据此使用公式。

```sh
python -m materials_boundaries catalog claims --id griffith_central_crack_plane_strain --json
```

foam states, literal coefficient-of-variance superscripts and statistical-group
letters. Unknown CV units are not inferred as percent or SD. Null typed
uncertainty does not mean the source reports no variation. Ten density samples
per group are preserved; independent production batches, repeat readings and
measurement age are unknown. The 24 h preparation cure and at least 7 day

# Offline formal-catalog overlap diagnostics

This standard-library-only command audits the pinned **1192 formal entries** and
compares explicitly supplied local clues. It addresses a gap in
`nomad_review_boundary`: that index checks the 1168 legacy bytes and count but
indexes only the computed composition groups. The existing catalog text search
does not search all reported composition text. The new command reuses the formal
catalog's admission pins, the existing composition parser, canonical hashes,
strict JSON decoding, canonical taxon keys and the reviewed wood crosswalk pin.
It creates no material, source adapter, candidate packet, approval request or
admission. It never fetches a URL or writes an input/catalog/cache file.

## Run locally

From this directory, using Python 3.11+:

```sh
python -B formal_overlap_audit.py > /absolute/local-evidence/field-coverage.json
python -B formal_overlap_audit.py --probes /absolute/local-evidence/probes.json \
  > /absolute/local-evidence/overlap-diagnostics.json
python -B -m unittest -v test_formal_overlap_audit
```

The output goes to stdout; choose a separate output path, never an input or
catalog file. Python bytecode writing is disabled before local imports. CLI
input is capped at 65,536 bytes and 20 probes; output is capped at 12,000,000
bytes, including its final newline. A failure exits 2 with a generic error and
no partial report. Duplicate JSON keys, unknown probe fields and nonfinite
numbers are refused. No package installation, credentials or network is needed.
This command reads the repository's explicitly pinned formal package resources;
a changed release fails closed rather than silently extending coverage.

Example diagnostic input (these are user-supplied clues, not provider records):

```json
{
  "schema": "formal-overlap-probes/1",
  "probes": [
    {"probe_id": "al2o3_formula_only", "formula": "Al2O3"},
    {"probe_id": "alumina_manual_hint", "formula": "Al2O3", "terms": ["alumina"]}
  ]
}
```

`alumina` is an explicit human search hint; it is not a synonym inferred from the
retained Alexandria fragment. The earlier fragment supplies the Al2O3 formula
only for this comparison and remains a reserialized, incomplete tool artifact.
It is not refreshed, imported, or promoted by this command.

## Field coverage and scope

Every formal ID appears once in `rows`, with its frozen identity-content digest,
source file label and JSON pointer. The mutually exclusive
`primary_comparability_partition` is:

| Primary comparison channel | Entries | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Structured integer composition | 24 | Reviewed computed composition and NOMAD references; phase/site-order and global equivalence remain unresolved. |
| Scoped canonical taxon identity | 1000 | Accepted WFO ID, tissue scope and historical backbone; no formula is inferred. |
| Advisory taxon crosswalk | 6 | Five conservative wood/culm exclusions and one cork-versus-wood non-merge rule; these do not repair or replace legacy taxonomy. |
| Source-qualified text only | 162 | Names, aliases, source/processing scope and sometimes grades or composition prose; no typed composition or canonical taxon key. |

These four classes sum to 1192. Separate field dimensions **overlap**: 159 legacy
entries have source-supported composition/purity prose, 31 have linked grades,
and 37 are composites. Do not add those dimensions to estimate coverage. All
1168 legacy identities lack a structured stoichiometric-composition field.
The prose is useful evidence for manual comparison, not a trustworthy machine
formula. Purity ranges, starting powders, additives, constituent ratios, supplier
grades, specimen state and final retained phases are different claims.

The five Tarasov PNA-BPF formulations contribute five qualified-text entries,
each with one DDS-cured state and no grade. Their nominal HCP:BPF:ECH feed
labels remain literal source prose, with inconsistent reagent entries and
unknown final composition. They do not become structured compositions or pure
molecular species, and a shared feed-label clue remains only a possible overlap.

The six Kapoor glasses add six source-qualified text entries and six linked
as-prepared states, no grades, and no structured stoichiometric composition.
Analyzed oxide mol% is not a nominal recipe or a pure-species assertion.

The two Tian composites add two source-qualified text entries, two as-extruded
states and no grades or structured compositions. Their nano-Ti loadings are
nominal, not analyzed final compositions; the unreinforced comparator is excluded.
They add no Al2O3 cue to the bounded check below.

`composition_prose_paths`, linked grade/state counts, canonical taxon fields,
crosswalk dispositions and source pointers identify exactly which formal records
have each channel. Each matched clue carries its path and qualifying identity,
state and composition notes. Evidence URLs, negative notes, identity-scope prose,
and unrelated source-scope comparisons are not positive search fields.

## Three diagnostic outcomes

- `confirmed_overlap`: the caller provides an exact formal ID **and** its
  frozen `identity_sha256`, with no conflicting supported probe facts. The
  `proof_scope` is `frozen_formal_record_reference`: this proves reuse of a
  catalog identity record, not that an external crystal/specimen is physically
  identical. Copying a public ID/hash does not authenticate the external claim.
- `possible_overlap`: a structured composition, provider/taxon reference,
  crosswalk or literal textual clue matches. This includes identical formulas
  for different structures, shared ingredients, grades from different suppliers,
  and same taxon with different tissue/backbone. Conflicts remain explicit;
  they are never resolved by choosing a convenient interpretation.
- `unable_to_compare`: no supported overlap evidence was found. This includes
  different structured values, missing fields and text that does not match the
  literal probe. It is **never** a new-material verdict or admission eligibility.

All results set `physical_equivalence` to `unasserted`, `new_material_count` to
null and `admitted_delta` to zero. The tool is not a complete chemical ontology,
structure matcher, taxonomic reconciliation engine or novelty detector.

The formula parser handles only simple integer stoichiometry and provides an
advisory reduced-composition key. Formula matches in legacy text are literal,
case-sensitive and word-bounded: `Co` does not match `CO`, and `Al2O3` does not
match `Al2O30`. Unsupported formulas are refused; compound names, product aliases
and grade strings are never parsed into structured composition. Caller-supplied
`terms` use case-insensitive literal matching and are clearly marked as such.
No stemming, synonym expansion or fuzzy matching is performed.

## Optional explicit reference clues

Each probe requires a unique `probe_id` and at least one comparison field.
Supported optional fields, with no extra keys, are:

- `formula`: a supported simple integer formula.
- `terms`: one to eight distinct literal phrases, each 2–80 characters.
- `formal_reference`: `{ "id": "...", "identity_sha256": "..." }`, copied
  from an audit row only for exact local record-reference diagnostics.
- `provider_reference`: `{ "provider": "nomad", "material_id": "..." }`
  and/or `entry_id`. Matching either is a source-reference relation, not a
  physical-equivalence or composition-bucket approval. Existing related-group
  links in the frozen formal review remain advisory and never create more
  formal entries. Material/entry pairs not present together are flagged.
- `taxon_reference`: `{ "accepted_taxon_id": "wfo-0000000000",
  "tissue_scope": "...", "backbone_sha256": "..." }`. A shared taxon remains
  a possible relation; tissue and backbone disagreement is retained.

Reference assertions are diagnostic input only. They do not register a provider
or grant trust. A differing formal digest cannot yield a confirmed match.
All probes and output rows are deterministically ordered; canonical input hashes
bind each probe without echoing arbitrary search terms into a new source record.

## The bounded Al2O3 check

A formula-only probe finds thirteen possible legacy relations and no confirmed
overlap: A16SG-derived alumina, an AlN/Y2O3/Al2O3 starting mixture, and a
Si3N4/Al2O3/Y2O3 starting mixture, four Bruns NBS2 glass formulations, and six
Kapoor calcium phosphate/aluminophosphate glasses.
The Bruns nominal oxide recipes and separate ICP-OES assays remain qualified
composition prose, not inferred pure stoichiometric compounds. No assay correction,
recipe normalization or final purity is inferred. Each recipe has one linked
furnace-cooled state; quenched states are excluded, and thermal history does not
create extra identities. Their actual composition text and qualification notes
remain attached. Kapoor uses analyzed ICP-OES mol% without normalization; its
three reported zero Al2O3 entries also match the literal text probe and do not
prove nonzero alumina content. Its annealed/reannealed as-prepared states
remain separate from excluded compressed states. None is treated as an ideal
pure Al2O3 crystal. The other
1172 entries are `unable_to_compare` for this probe; that count is a diagnostic
coverage gap, not a count of novel materials or an assertion that overlap is
impossible. No new Alexandria network read is performed.

The complete output inventories only formal 1168 + 24 entries. The 62 excluded
examples, the older seven examples, related provider groups and calculation
counts are never added to the formal total. This local diagnosis changes no
scientific, licensing or admission decision and generates no approval workflow.

These are the appended experimental catalog boundaries at data commit
`e6d39e39184ab333045ae3ae2d001ab6b41bd53f`.
Previously retained 1081-entry, 1103-entry, 1107-entry, 1108-entry, 1114-entry, 1116-entry, 1124-entry, 1127-entry, 1133-entry, 1136-entry, 1148-entry, 1168-entry, 1172-entry, 1177-entry, 1183-entry and 1185-entry diagnostic reports
remain historical evidence and are not rewritten.

# Offline formal-review gap report

`formal_review_gaps.py` produces a deterministic, machine-readable deficiency
report for the held `AlGa2Sc` and `O8Re2Ru4` review priority. It reuses the exact
historically accepted second-tranche metadata and identifies evidence still
unverified for a new formal release. It makes no source request, performs no
directory search, and creates no approval or admission.

The 62-record historical metadata acceptance remains intact: 47 metal-family
and 15 inorganic examples, all outside the formal catalog. The proposed two-row
subset is always **held**, with **zero formal admissions** from this command.
Current experimental counts are **1192 = 1168 + 24**; the separate `CaEr2Eu` candidate remains
held. Original input, review, acceptance pins and formal resources are read-only.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, using Python 3.11+:

```sh
python experimental/platform/ingestion/formal_review_gaps.py > /absolute/local-evidence/formal-review-gaps.json
```

Create the output directory beforehand and keep generated reports outside the
checkout. The command writes UTF-8 JSON to standard output; shell redirection writes
the report. There is no output-path option. An alternate checkout can be selected
explicitly:

```sh
python experimental/platform/ingestion/formal_review_gaps.py --repo-root /absolute/materials-boundaries-checkout > /absolute/local-evidence/formal-review-gaps.json
```

`--repo-root` does not accept a replacement trust policy. The selected checkout
must contain the exact trusted artifacts. Changed source bytes, modified pins or
unexpected selected-record identities fail the binding checks.

An exit code of `0` means the held report was generated; it is not approval or a
readiness pass. An exit code of `2` indicates an argument or source-binding error.
The report schema is `formal-admission-gaps/1`. Repeating the command with the same
bound inputs and local artifact bytes yields the same report; there is no live
query, current-time observation or automatically changing provider state.

## Optional local artifact checks

Supply an existing file only when its role is known. Repeat `--artifact LABEL=PATH`
to compare that file's SHA-256 with the corresponding historical reference:

```sh
python experimental/platform/ingestion/formal_review_gaps.py --artifact frozen_source_response_sha256=/absolute/private-evidence/source-snapshot.json --artifact attribution_response_sha256=/absolute/private-evidence/attribution-snapshot.json > /absolute/local-evidence/formal-review-gaps-with-artifacts.json
```

For a path containing spaces, quote the complete `LABEL=PATH` argument. These are
explicit local filesystem paths, not URLs or download instructions. The command
does not discover files, retrieve missing snapshots or upload their contents.
Each supplied target is checked for regular-file status before opening it for
reading. A regular file is hashed only if it is at most 32,000,000 bytes; one
extra byte may be read to detect an oversized file. Raw contents and local file
paths are not included in the report. Do not commit or publish raw evidence
merely to make an availability check pass. Unknown or repeated labels are
argument errors.

Supported labels distinguish the five per-record evidence references from the
two other historical acceptance references:

| Artifact label | Historical reference |
| --- | --- |
| `candidate_packet_sha256` | Selected record's candidate packet |
| `archive_response_sha256` | Selected record's archive response |
| `relations_response_sha256` | Selected record's relation response |
| `frozen_source_response_sha256` | Selected record's frozen source response |
| `attribution_response_sha256` | Selected record's attribution response |
| `source_unit_definition_snapshot_sha256` | Acceptance pin's unit-definition snapshot |
| `acceptance_candidate_file_sha256` | Acceptance pin's candidate file |

`candidate_packet_sha256` and `acceptance_candidate_file_sha256` are distinct
references; do not substitute one file for the other based on a similar name.
The two selected records share their five per-record reference hashes, which
makes a small explicitly supplied evidence set useful for both.

Each `evidence_observations` item records its expected hash, parent JSON pointers,
availability, actual hash when computed and bytes read:

| `availability` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `reference_only_not_provided` | No local file was supplied for this reference. |
| `missing` | The explicitly supplied local file was not found. |
| `not_regular_file` | The supplied target is a directory, FIFO, device or other non-regular file; its contents are not opened. |
| `read_error` | The file could not be read; local paths and OS error details are omitted. |
| `size_limit_exceeded` | The size probe exceeded the permitted hashing bound. |
| `digest_match` | Supplied bytes match the historical hash reference. |
| `digest_mismatch` | Supplied bytes do not match that reference. |

These observations are reported with exit code `0` when the trusted parent
bindings are valid; they do not make the report an approval or failure verdict.
A matching digest proves equality to the recorded bytes; it does not authenticate
the original reviewer, establish license ownership, repeat geometry diagnostics
or approve a new release. Even if every supplied file matches, the new formal
release remains held.

## Read the report without upgrading its claims

The report binds the parent input, normalized review, canonical review,
acceptance pin and each selected normalized record to trusted exact hashes. It
also checks the pinned formal/review boundary, including the formal 24 and the
unadmitted 62. These bindings prevent a locally rewritten review from silently
becoming the trusted source of its own approval.

The selected metadata is identified as historical parent-review content. Its

# Resumable NOMAD review-queue updates

`nomad_incremental.py` extends the existing bounded NOMAD collector and candidate
normalizer. It maintains a local observation baseline and produces a reviewable
delta after each complete acquisition cycle. It uses Python 3.11+ and the standard
library; it does not require a service, account or credentials.

Automatic acquisition is not scientific review, license clearance or admission.
The current experiment's formal project total is **1192 = 1168 legacy identities + 24 reviewed
computed composition buckets**. The 62 unadmitted computed examples, the older
seven-record example and their known related provider IDs are excluded from new
candidate admission claims. This command never changes the formal catalog.
Candidate groups and calculations contribute **zero** admissions and do not count
toward the goal of at least 1000 materials in each of five categories.

The current boundary names the exact data commit
`e6d39e39184ab333045ae3ae2d001ab6b41bd53f` and binds the exact appended experimental
catalog bytes plus the unchanged 24-reviewed/62-excluded example resources. Use a new state directory when moving from an earlier
1081-entry, 1103-entry, 1107-entry, 1108-entry, 1114-entry, 1116-entry, 1124-entry, 1127-entry, 1133-entry, 1136-entry, 1142-entry, 1148-entry, 1158-entry, 1166-entry, 1167-entry, 1168-entry, 1172-entry, 1177-entry, 1183-entry, 1185-entry or 1188-entry boundary. `update` and `abandon` reject a different
stored scope before dispatching a request, charging a budget or changing cycle
state; they never migrate an old store silently. `status`, `report` and `compare`
remain read-only and retain the saved scope, so historical 1081-entry,
1103-entry, 1107-entry, 1108-entry, 1114-entry, 1116-entry, 1124-entry, 1127-entry, 1133-entry, 1136-entry, 1142-entry, 1148-entry, 1158-entry, 1166-entry, 1167-entry, 1168-entry, 1172-entry, 1177-entry, 1183-entry, 1185-entry and 1188-entry reports are not relabeled as 1192. Saved-report counts
must agree with that store's hash-bound boundary. Explicit Python boundary injection is available for
synthetic test identities only within the same exact pinned scope; the CLI has
no boundary override or bypass flag.

## Compare cached source fields offline

After two cycles have completed, compare their cached observations without another
provider request or a store write:

```sh
python nomad_incremental.py compare /absolute/local-data/nomad-small --before 1 --after 2 > /absolute/local-data/nomad-source-changes.json
```

Use cycle IDs from `status`. Both IDs are required, positive, and ordered
(`before < after`); missing, incomplete and abandoned cycles are refused. The
cycles need not be adjacent. Both are read within one read-only SQLite snapshot
using the existing profile, boundary and response-integrity checks. This command
does not acquire, retry, abandon or advance a cycle, alter a review, or admit a
candidate. Exit `0` means a comparison was produced; exit `2` means an invalid
request, evidence/binding error or an exceeded comparison limit. No partial
comparison is printed on failure. Keep output outside the checkout.

Comparison supports the collector's default rollback-journal SQLite stores.
Externally converted WAL-mode stores are refused after a read-only header probe,
before opening SQLite: SQLite `mode=ro` alone can create WAL/SHM coordination
files. The command does not change journal mode, checkpoint, restore, or ignore
WAL contents. Do not change journal mode or replace store files concurrently.
Other existing ingestion operations retain their original behavior.

The compact JSON schema is `nomad-evidence-compare/1`. It avoids manually opening
two large responses to locate a changed density, unit, source, method or author:

- `before_cycle` and `after_cycle` bind the saved cycle and report with canonical
  hashes, plus the exact successful response attempts, endpoints, byte counts,
  request hashes and response-byte hashes. Profile and boundary hashes identify
  the fixed collection scope. These hashes are local content bindings, not
  authentication of the source, reviewer or database administrator.
- `entry_changes` compares every observed entry, including held entries and
  nonrepresentative calculations. Each side retains all archive and attribution
  variant hashes and the **recorded** gate reasons. Gate payload hashes bind the
  complete original exclusions. The command reads saved complete reports; it
  does not regenerate an old report against today's observation baseline or
  issue a new eligibility decision.
- `fields` locates selected differences with `source` (`archive` or
  `attribution`) and a JSON Pointer relative to the corresponding response's
  `data` row. Each side has explicit presence, JSON type and canonical value
  hash. Small nonsensitive scalar values are included exactly as decoded,
  preserving null, string/number distinctions and units. Missing and null remain distinct.
  These are decoded JSON values, not the original lexical number spelling.
- The selected fields cover source/processing metadata, formula/elements,
  provider identity, structural type, space-group number, method/program labels,
  scalar density, explicit unit labels, dimensionality, author names, references
  and dataset identifiers/names/DOIs. Lists retain index order. This is a fixed
  review aid, not an exhaustive scientific projection or raw-asset export.
  No arbitrary method, symmetry, author or dataset subtree is copied into output.
- `mainfile`, reference items and DOI locators are always hash-only, including
  apparently public URLs: no pathname, userinfo, signed query or fragment is
  copied from those fields. Other strings with path/URI/assignment/control syntax,
  recognized credential markers or an unbroken word over 64 characters are also
  hash-only. The only slash exceptions are `kg/m^3` and `g/cm^3` at the explicit
  density-unit fields; this preserves a wrong-unit observation without converting
  it. Ordinary scientific labels and author names remain visible. Unsafe output
  IDs, gate labels and unknown input-event codes in saved reports are refused
  with a generic error. Local store paths and environment variables are not
  included in output. This conservative guard may withhold harmless strings; it
  is not a universal secret detector or authorization to use a private store.
  Use only the existing public-metadata acquisition stores, never credentials
  or private data disguised as scientific values or provider identifiers.
- Conflicting archive or attribution variants are listed in `ambiguous_entries`.
  A changed ambiguous entry has `source_comparison: ambiguous_variants` and no
  paired fields; it requires inspecting the bound source evidence. Identical
  duplicate rows coalesce as in the existing ingestion report.
- `unexpanded_source_change` conservatively stays `true` for every changed source
  fingerprint, even when selected fields explain some changes. Unknown fields,
  containers, oversized scalars and long lists retain hash-only observations;
  an empty `fields` list is never proof that the source did not change.
- `candidate_changes` compares saved candidate-queue semantic hashes, excluding
  retrieval evidence as in the existing incremental delta. Entry changes can
  occur without a candidate change, for example for a nonrepresentative
  calculation. Repeated identical input yields empty change lists. Separate
  cycle/report bindings still differ because they identify separate acquisitions.

`recorded_after_input_events` preserves events relative to the later cycle's
then-current baseline, which may not be the selected earlier cycle. An entry
observed only before/after the comparison is not a confirmed upstream deletion
or new material. A `withdrawal_pending_review` event and removal from the
candidate queue do not revoke a formal record. Comparison does not reuse or
authenticate a prior scientific review or scoped rights decision.

The output is bounded to 2,000,000 UTF-8 bytes, with at most 2,000 distinct entry
IDs. Scalars over 2,048 canonical UTF-8 bytes are hash-only. Lists of over 100
items are hash-only without expanding their elements; shorter lists also carry
a parent hash. An exceeded entry or output limit refuses the whole comparison.
The existing integrity check still verifies all retained raw responses in the
store; comparison limits do not establish a bound on total retained history.
`comparison_sha256` hashes the canonical result before adding that field, so it
differs from the stdout file hash. Identical stored inputs and cycle selection
produce identical stdout bytes. Concurrent reads describe their transaction's
snapshot, not subsequent updates. The report is local review evidence; inspect
source-specific scope before any redistribution.

Comparisons retain their store's formal total: **1192 = 1168 + 24** for a new
current store, or the saved historical total for an older store. The **62 examples stay excluded**.
`admitted_delta` is always `0` and `release_authorized` is always `false`.
The comparison is separate from the existing formal-review gap report and does
not close its scientific, identity, authority or reuse requirements.

## Collection scope

Initialize one immutable profile per store. The default profile revisits one page
of two public OQMD bulk entries, ordered by `entry_id`, on every complete cycle.
`--after` fixes the starting cursor; subsequent page cursors are persisted while
that cycle runs. The next cycle restarts at the configured starting cursor so
changes to previously observed entries can be detected. It does not automatically
walk the entire provider dataset or represent a transactional snapshot.

Alternatively, repeat `--entry-id` to follow a small, fixed public entry cohort.
The unique cohort must fit `--page-size`, with `--pages 1` and no `--after`.
Exact-ID responses still undergo the OQMD origin and all other eligibility gates.

Previously observed IDs missing from the new window receive bounded, public
exact-ID archive checks. Only a validated, exhaustive exact-ID response can mark
an ID `withdrawal_pending_review`. That state means the public query did not
return it; it does not prove deletion or revoke an approved material. An entry
that moves outside the scanned window but remains publicly readable is retained
through these rechecks. A changed or reappearing record is reported separately.
Rechecks share the same cycle budget, so a growing observation history can exhaust
that budget instead of silently expanding acquisition.

## Reproduce a small local cycle

Run from `experimental/platform/ingestion`. Choose a persistent local store
outside the checkout; the following paths are examples.

```sh
python nomad_incremental.py init /absolute/local-data/nomad-small --pages 1 --page-size 2 --max-requests 8 --max-bytes 2000000 --max-response 500000 --retries 1
python nomad_incremental.py update /absolute/local-data/nomad-small
python nomad_incremental.py status /absolute/local-data/nomad-small
python nomad_incremental.py report /absolute/local-data/nomad-small > /absolute/local-data/nomad-small-report.json
python nomad_incremental.py report /absolute/local-data/nomad-small --cycle 1 > /absolute/local-data/nomad-small-cycle-1.json
```

`init`, `status`, `report` and `abandon` are offline commands. Only `update`
performs public network reads. Output is JSON on standard output; argument or
store errors are written to standard error. In PowerShell, use a Windows path
such as `C:\local-data\materials-boundaries\nomad-small` in place of the example
store path.

`status` includes a `history` list with each cycle's `id`, `status`, `requests`,
`bytes_charged` and `started_utc`, alongside the latest cycle state. Use one of
those IDs with `report STORE --cycle N` to retrieve an earlier cycle's report
offline. Omitting `--cycle` selects the latest cycle; a nonexistent cycle is an
error. Completed and abandoned reports remain available after later updates.

To configure a fixed cohort, initialize a separate store and replace the example
IDs with verified public NOMAD entry IDs:

```sh
python nomad_incremental.py init /absolute/local-data/nomad-cohort --pages 1 --page-size 2 --entry-id ENTRY_ID_1 --entry-id ENTRY_ID_2 --max-requests 8 --max-bytes 2000000 --max-response 500000 --retries 1
python nomad_incremental.py update /absolute/local-data/nomad-cohort
```

Rerun `update` on the same store. If the previous cycle completed, this starts a
new bounded cycle and compares its source content with the committed baseline.
Unchanged input yields no input or candidate delta, even though the new cycle has
its own retrieval evidence and timestamps. If the previous cycle is incomplete,
the command resumes it using the durable cursor and successful response cache.
Partial cycles never advance the committed baseline.

The example limits above are also the defaults. Supported limits are:

| Option | Meaning | Allowed range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--pages` | Initial window page limit | 1..10 |
| `--page-size` | Maximum entries per request | 1..100 |
| `--max-requests` | HTTP attempts per cycle, including retries and rechecks | 1..32 |
| `--max-bytes` | Total charged response bytes per cycle | 1..30,000,000 |
| `--max-response` | Response byte limit, no larger than `--max-bytes` | 1..3,000,000 |
| `--retries` | Additional attempts per logical request | 0..3 |

The HTTP timeout is 30 seconds. An interrupted in-flight request keeps its
reserved request count and response-byte allowance charged, even if no response
was committed. This conservative accounting prevents restarts from restoring
spent budget. A size-limit probe may read one extra byte to detect overflow and
then rejects that response; it does not accept an oversized response as evidence.
The profile cannot be overwritten by repeating `init`. Any intentional new scope
or limits require a separate store and a separately reviewed acquisition plan.

## Recovery and scheduling behavior

The store contains `incremental.sqlite3` and `.update.lock`. SQLite persists the
profile and its hash, the pinned review boundary and its hash, cycle state,
request reservations, exact accepted response bytes and hashes, acquisition
records, and the last complete observation baseline. An archive response is
committed before its attribution request; a restart can reuse it. Keep the whole
store for audit and recovery, and back it up only when no update is running.

An exclusive, nonblocking OS file lock permits one writer per store. A concurrent
writer is rejected, and the OS releases the lock after process termination. The
presence of `.update.lock` alone is not a stale-lock error; deleting it is not a
recovery procedure. Use local storage with working SQLite and OS locking.

| Result | CLI exit code | Operator action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complete `update` | `0` | Inspect the report; the next update starts a new cycle. |
| Paused or cooldown `update` | `2` | Inspect `status`; rerun after the recorded cooldown, if any. |
| Exhausted or blocked `update` | `2` | Investigate and explicitly abandon the incomplete cycle if a new attempt is appropriate. |
| Invalid arguments, invalid store or lock conflict | `2` | Correct the reported error; no successful cycle is implied. |
| Successful offline command | `0` | Inspect its JSON output; this does not imply acquisition completed. |

HTTP 429 and 503 responses persist representable `Retry-After` values as an
absolute cooldown, including HTTP-date values. Numeric delays outside the
platform's UTC range block the cycle without a shorter fallback or automatic
retry; the attempted request remains charged. The command returns without
waiting through that cooldown. A
repeated job during cooldown performs no new request. Public requests also use a
persisted last-dispatch time for one-second request spacing; this pacing may
sleep for up to one second. Transport failures retain the partial cycle;
remaining attempts are consumed only by later invocations. Per-request retries
and cycle budgets persist across process restarts. Repeated scheduling must not
silently reset exhausted budgets or abandon failed cycles.

After investigating a blocked or exhausted cycle, an operator may explicitly
record abandonment:

```sh
python nomad_incremental.py abandon /absolute/local-data/nomad-small --reason "Reviewed incomplete cycle; author endpoint failed within the fixed retry budget"
python nomad_incremental.py update /absolute/local-data/nomad-small
```

Abandonment preserves the cycle, evidence and reason, leaves the last complete
baseline unchanged, and permits the next `update` to start a new bounded cycle.
The provider cooldown survives abandonment. Do not put `abandon` in a recurring
job or treat it as a way to bypass `Retry-After`.

## Local scheduling examples

These examples describe optional operator setup; this implementation installs no
schedule. Initialize the store and inspect a manual run before scheduling the
same `update` command. Hourly examples keep acquisition small; each invocation
remains subject to the persisted profile, retry limits and cooldown. There is no
cloud scheduler, deployment, credential generation or permission change.

For Windows Task Scheduler, replace the no-space executable, checkout and store
paths below with the actual local paths. This is an example registration command,
not an action performed by the project:

```powershell
schtasks.exe /Create /TN "Materials Boundaries Incremental Review" /SC HOURLY /MO 1 /TR "C:\Python311\python.exe C:\src\materials-boundaries-public\experimental\platform\ingestion\nomad_incremental.py update C:\local-data\materials-boundaries\nomad-small"
```

For paths containing spaces, configure the action in Task Scheduler with the
Python executable in **Program/script** and the quoted script and store paths in
**Add arguments**, for example:

```text
"C:\work projects\materials-boundaries-public\experimental\platform\ingestion\nomad_incremental.py" update "C:\local data\materials-boundaries\nomad-small"
```

Choose **Do not start a new instance** if the task is already running. The store
lock also protects manual/scheduled overlap. Task Scheduler result `0x2` requires
checking the offline `status` or `report`; it may mean a persisted cooldown or a
blocked cycle, not an empty successful update. Task history alone is not the
acquisition audit record.

For Linux cron, an equivalent hourly crontab entry is:

```cron
0 * * * * /usr/bin/python3 /srv/materials-boundaries-public/experimental/platform/ingestion/nomad_incremental.py update /var/local/materials-boundaries/nomad-small >> /var/local/materials-boundaries/nomad-small-job.log 2>&1
```

Use an existing writable local directory and a Python 3.11+ executable. The log
collects separate JSON reports across runs and is not itself one JSON document.
Inspect `report` for a single current report. Neither scheduler example performs
scientific approval or modifies catalog entries.

## Review the delta and evidence

`report` verifies stored evidence hashes and reads the selected cycle without a
network request. A completed report is retained with the cycle; an incomplete
report is provisional and must not be treated as a committed update. Historical
reports preserve their recorded state and cooldown, while `status` reports the
current store cooldown. Review:

- `complete`, `baseline_committed`, `status` and `stop_reason` before any counts.
